size.note: Sexed head-and-body length and tail length follow Wikipedia: males 78–108 cm with tails of 21–34 cm; females 71–103 cm with tails of 18–31.5 cm (female tail max rounded to 32 cm). Wikipedia gives male mass of 7.2–19 kg (n=77) and female mass of 7–15.9 kg (n=63). Animal Diversity Web gives a shorter unsexed head-and-body length of 62–91 cm, tails of 18–34 cm, and mass of 8–19 kg, with females typically at or below 13 kg and males up to 20 kg. The Wikipedia sexed ranges are entered; the ADW disagreement is noted. No published shoulder-height range was found.

summary: A medium-sized, plain reddish cat with long, black-tufted ears and a short tail. It is seldom seen in Kruger, where leopards and other large carnivores are common.
description: The coat is brown to red, usually paler in females, with a white, lightly spotted underside. The face has black marks on the whisker pads and around and above the eyes, and a faint dark line down the centre of the head and nose. The ears are tall, with long black tufts, and are the species' most distinctive mark. The hind legs are long and well muscled, and the tail is short. Eye colour ranges from golden or copper to green or grey. Young animals have shorter ear tufts and blue-tinted eyes. Melanistic individuals have been reported but are very rare.
habits: Mostly solitary, and mainly nocturnal, though it may be seen by day. It is a powerful jumper and takes much of its prey, including birds, with a leap. In protected areas with large carnivores it is thought to suffer interference competition, especially from leopards, which have been recorded killing caracals. In Kruger and the adjoining private reserves it is seen less often than on farmland, and appears to be more common in mixed Combretum woodland on granite landscapes.

diet.summary: A carnivore that takes a wide range of prey, from rodents, hares, birds and reptiles up to small antelope such as steenbok, and it can kill animals larger than itself, including black-backed jackal. It is an opportunistic hunter rather than a specialist.

young: Juveniles have shorter ear tufts and blue-tinted eyes. No Kruger-specific birth-month range, litter size or gestation figure was entered from the sources consulted in this session. Skinner and Chimimba (2005, p. 401) say litters are recorded in every month, with births peaking from October to February; the mean gestation is 79 days (range 78–81) and litters average about 2.2 young (range 1–3).
habitat: A wide range of habitats with cover, from semi-arid scrub and woodland to more open savanna; it avoids true desert and closed tropical forest. In Kruger it is scarce and appears to favour mixed Combretum woodland on the granite landscapes.

similar.note: The African wild cat is much smaller, lacks long black ear tufts, and has a sandy-grey, faintly striped coat and a ringed tail with a black tip.
The serval has a spotted and striped coat, a small head, very long legs and large ears without long black tufts.

population.notes: No Kruger population figure was found. The EWT 2025 assessment says caracals are less frequently observed in Kruger and the adjoining private reserves, where they appear more common in mixed Combretum woodland on granite, and may be limited by competition with leopards.

viewNotes.note: A plain reddish coat, long hind legs, a short tail, and tall ears with long black tufts.
The face shows black marks around the eyes and long black ear tufts.

calls.description: A distinctive cough-like call has been reported in a mating context. A general field call of the species was not described in the sources consulted.
